answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally verifiable stake in a shared vault before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. The kernel caps each stake’s influence and slashes it when challenge audits show coordinated, fabricated activity; a falcon monitor can flag suspicious clusters for those audits, but flags alone do not prove guilt. Spawning a thousand identities therefore means tying up a thousand stakes and risking forfeiture, making a sybil attack costly rather than merely requiring more accounts.
